transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-02-08 15:00 UTC | Duration 55m | Attendees: Maya, Ethan, Rosa (Redwood) + Aaron, Samir, Jules, Tina (Nightingale)

Summary: quick kickoff to map quality goals to measurable tests. talked budget constraints, dedicated vs hosted, and security gating.

[00:00] Maya (Redwood): hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro — i'm maya, i'm the AE on this. ethan and rosa are with me from solutions. can you each say hi?
[00:10] Dr. Aaron Li (Nightingale): hi, aaron here. CTO. we want to nail hallucination rates in our clinical summarization flow, and also format adherence for export to EHR.
[00:22] Samir Rao (Nightingale): samir, i own ml infra. we have about 12k daily queries for the pilot path, p95 latency needs to be <700ms ideally.
[00:35] Maya (Redwood): great, and the goal of this call especially is to align on acceptance criteria and the actual tests we'll run during the poc, so we can scope the bench and timeline.
[00:48] Ethan (Redwood SE): quick clarifying Q — when you say format adherence, is that strictly field-level JSON schema conformance, or also downstream CSV/EHR mapping?
[00:58] Jules Park (Nightingale Product): mostly JSON schema today, but yes we do map to CCD fields; so if the model drops fields or changes date formats that's a fail.
[01:12] Tina (Security): on the security side we'll need audit logs, KMS-backed key storage, and SSO via SAML. also curious about data retention and any logs redwood keeps.
[01:26] Rosa (Redwood): noted, we have SOC2 + ISO, and we can provide the compliance pack. for private deploy we support customer-managed KMS.
[01:36] Dr. Aaron Li: ok good. now on hallucinations — our tolerance is low. we have a clinical accuracy metric that must be above 98% on gold cases, and hallucinations must be <1% on production style prompts.
[01:52] Maya: i want to propose a two-track scoring: automated checks for format and hallucination heuristics, plus a human review for a sample set — that will be our acceptance gate.
[02:05] Samir: makes sense. what's the size of the golden set you recommend?
[02:09] Ethan: typically we recommend 200-400 golden prompts that capture happy path + edge cases + adversarial cases. for regression we usually run 300-500 examples per sprint depending on variance.
[02:21] Jules: we can pull 250 representative queries from prod logs, anonymize them, and annotate expected outputs.
[02:29] Maya: perfect. scoring approach — propose weighted metrics: format conformance 40%, factual accuracy/hallucination 40%, latency/cost 20%.each has thresholds.
[02:41] Dr. Aaron Li: i'm wary of the latency weight; our SLA is strict. can we translate the 20% into concrete numbers?
[02:47] Ethan: yes: target p50 <300ms, p95 <700ms for hosted with caching; token cost per 1k tokens should be under agreed pilot budget, we will surface per-token pricing.
[02:58] Samir: caching — do you support KV cache across requests? we've got long contexts with reference docs.
[03:04] Rosa: yes we support prefix and KV caching; note that across private deployments you can control cache residency.
[03:12] Jules: how about quantization? will quantized models affect hallucination rates?
[03:16] Ethan: small risk — we usually recommend a quality run comparing fp16 baseline vs 8-bit quantized. and we run a hallucination delta test to detect regressions.
[03:27] Dr. Aaron Li: okay timeline — we have compliance review windows. ideally pilot starts 2027-02-22 and runs 6 weeks, does that match expectations?
[03:36] Maya: yes 6-week POC is standard: week 0 onboarding + baseline bench, weeks 1-4 iterative tuning and regression sprints, week 5 acceptance and wrap.
[03:47] Tina: onboarding is heavy for us — need a private deployment checklist for networking and firewall rules.
[03:53] Rosa: we'll send a private-deploy network checklist. also, for hosted we can usually spin up sandbox in 48 hours.
[04:02] Ethan: bench plan details — we'll run three model variants: 1) baseline open model, 2) tuned variant with prompt engineering, 3) quantized candidate. For each variant we'll capture: latency P50/P95, tokens per response, failure modes, hallucination rate by automated classifier, and human-sampled precision.
[04:24] Dr. Aaron Li: how do you compute hallucination automatically? that's a tricky one.
[04:29] Ethan: we use a combination of LLM-based fact-checking heuristics and deterministic string checks for expected fields. it's noisy — hence the human review overlay. we'll produce confidence scores per example.
[04:40] Samir: and regression testing cadence?
[04:43] Maya: we recommend weekly regression runs against the golden set plus daily synthetic smoke tests for throughput. major rollbacks if hallucination spikes >0.5% week-over-week.
[04:57] Jules: do you have a standard scoring rubric we can reuse?
[05:00] Maya: yes — we'll share the rubric. high level: pass/fail per sample for format, factual score 0-1, and aggregate weighted score. acceptance threshold: aggregate weighted >= 0.92 for pilot sign-off (configurable).
[05:15] Tina: can we see example reports?
[05:18] Rosa: yes we'll attach a sample report that shows per-example flags, hallucination likelihood, and a regression delta chart.
[05:25] Dr. Aaron Li: cost — if we hit production volumes after POC, do you offer reserved/dedicated pricing?
[05:31] Maya: yes, we can propose dedicated capacity with predictable throughput and a commit. we'll include both hosted and dedicated price lanes in the pricing worksheet.
[05:40] Samir: one more technical Q — does redwood support pinned model versions and automatic fallback?
[05:45] Ethan: yes, we support model pinning and smart routing. fallback to a compatible variant in the same family is built-in if capacity constrained.
[05:55] Maya: ok circling back to deliverables: we'll send the golden-prompt template, scoring rubric, compliance pack, network checklist, and a proposed bench plan. customer to provide golden and regression sets.
[06:08] Jules: agreed. small note — for golden prompts we will include some synthetic adversarial examples.
[06:15] Ethan: that's good — we want those to stress-test hallucination checks.
[06:20] Dr. Aaron Li: what about edge-case hallucinations tied to patient identifiers? we can't leak PII in tests.
[06:27] Tina: we will fully de-id data; samir will handle anonymization pipeline and share hash mapping offline.
[06:34] Maya: timeline recap: Maya sends docs by 2/12, Ethan posts bench results baseline by 2/15, customer sends examples by 2/14, deep-dive for private deploy week of 2/18, pilot start 2/22.
[06:50] Samir: sounds good. any blockers?
[06:53] Tina: only the compliance sign-off, but we expect it to be OK with docs.
[06:57] Maya: great — last thing, do we want to include a golden prompt scoring workshop with product + se? might speed annotation.
[07:03] Jules: yes please, that'll help.
[07:07] Maya: ok we'll put that on the calendar.
[07:10] Dr. Aaron Li: thanks all.
[07:13] Maya: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the artifacts.

Notes (imperfections): occasional transcription errors: "K V cash" vs "KV cache" appears in some lines, some names misattributed as Speaker 5 in the raw export, punctuation is uneven.

End of transcript.
notes: Customer emphasized very low hallucination tolerance for clinical summaries and format conformance for EHR exports. Agreed weighted scoring rubric and 6-week POC timeline. Need de-identified golden set and SOC2 docs.
